title: Trader-restart Telegram ping: selective, sectioned, status headline, cause line, live-trade accounting
note: Lane session_01LtduMwXcSLF2D7F6L3Xgyj. Built: one restart ping (status headline, cause line, per-venue expandable sections, per-account broker-vs-journal reconcile with MEASURED SL/TP), compact 2-line form for a clean deploy/manual restart. Cause evidence: restart-intent marker (deploy/manual/watchdog) + systemd journal of previous exit + host uptime. Tier 2, landing hold. Proposed (NOT built, separate Tier-2 question): keep the trader up across deploys whose runtime diff touches only web-api/other-unit code. MERGED 2026-10-15T09:40Z (PR #18226). NOT yet observed. Closes when: the first trader restart after deploy logs 'boot_audit: restart report' and the Telegram SYSTEM ping shows a cause line 'deploy <sha> (#PR)' (or an evidenced cause), per-account counts matching /api/diag positions, no false ghost/untracked from IB/Alpaca symbol mismatch. If cause reads 'unknown' on a deploy, check journalctl readability for the trader user. Proposed, not built: skip restarting ict-trader-live on deploys that touch no trader-imported code (separate Tier-2). TIER-2 PROPOSAL (not built; for the operator): skip restarting ict-trader-live when a deploy's runtime diff touches nothing the trader loads. DESIGN: deploy_pull_restart.sh already computes RUNTIME_CHANGES (diff vs deployed_sha.txt). Add a per-unit gate for ict-trader-live ONLY: restart it iff some changed path is (a) a .py in the trader's STATIC import closure from src.main (AST walk incl. function-level imports + import_module literals; MEASURED 2026-10-15: 382 files), or (b) ANY non-.py runtime path (config/, deploy/, requirements*, pyproject, comms/ outside the safe set, tools/), or (c) a .py outside src/ and scripts/. Only src/**.py and scripts/**.py outside the closure skip it. Other units (web-api, telegram bot, timers) keep restarting as today. The closure is generated by a script and committed (e.g. config/trader_import_closure.txt); a CI guard recomputes it and fails on drift, the same lockstep pattern as the scripts/research in-process list. Fail-safe: a missing or unreadable closure file means restart. deployed_sha.txt still advances, so the trader is never left on stale code it actually loads. RISKS: (1) dynamic imports the AST walk cannot see (getattr/importlib with computed names) could leave the trader on stale code; mitigated by (b) and (c), the drift guard, and a whitelist test of known dynamic loaders. (2) A subprocess a trader-loaded module runs (scripts/*.py invoked from src/) is not an import, so it is picked up fresh on each call anyway; no staleness. (3) deployed_sha now means web-api deployed while the trader may run older but behaviour-identical code; the boot ping's cause line and diag restart_pending must read per-unit. FREQUENCY, MEASURED over first-parent merges to main 2026-10-08T09:40Z..2026-10-15T09:40Z (n=879): 711 non-runtime (already skip), 168 runtime (restart today), of which 42 (25%) touch only non-closure src/scripts .py (web-api routers, scripts/ops tools, research_catalog) and would SKIP the trader restart; 126 still restart. Merges are batched per ~5-min sync tick, so actual restarts are <= these counts. Top restart-forcing paths among the 126: src/prop 26, scripts/ops (in closure) 14, src/runtime 14, comms/claude_strategy_scores.jsonl 8, comms/live_parity 7, comms/strategy_reviews 7, tools/phone-executor 6, comms/cloud 5. PHASE 2 (also needs proof): comms/cloud, comms/strategy_reviews and comms/claude_strategy_scores.jsonl have NO textual reference in the trader closure (grep 2026-10-15). A data-file reader map would move up to ~20 more merges to skip, but a path built at runtime must be ruled out first.
